scenarios.title: Offer high support for a low cycle
scenarios.objective: Maintain a separated high outlet while teammates cycle low in the attacking zone.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net. F1 carries behind the goal line; F2 supports along the side and YOU arrive high. Gold 1 guards the slot, Gold 2 watches the higher lane, and Gold 3 protects space near the net.
cues: F1 controls below the Gold net.

questions.prompt: Which Navy forward controls the puck behind Gold’s goal line?

options.text: F1
F2
YOU

questions.explanation: F1 controls the puck behind the attacking goal line.

questions.prompt: Which two details support a high outlet?

options.text: Whether F1 can reach a high support option
Gold 1's slot coverage
Following F2 into the same low space

questions.explanation: Carrier visibility and the slot defender shape the value of a separated high outlet.

questions.prompt: Arrange a high-outlet read.

options.text: Locate F1, F2 and the slot defender
Offer a separated high lane
Re-check the carrier and point-side pressure

questions.explanation: The outlet remains useful only when the carrier and pressure can connect to it.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a high support point separate from F2.
questions.explanation: The example stays nearer the blue line than F1 and F2. It moves farther from Gold 2 but nearer Gold 1, so recheck both before asking for a pass.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 leaves the slot to pressure the puck. What should YOU weigh?

options.text: An inside connection if F1 can reach it, or hold high if Gold 2 covers
Drop beside F2 without checking the slot
Shoot because the slot defender moved

questions.explanation: Gold 1 leaving can open an inside branch, but F1’s passing route and Gold 2’s coverage still need a scan.

questions.prompt: How does a high outlet help a low cycle?
questions.explanation: It gives F1 a separated option and can make Gold choose between the slot and the carrier. If the route is covered, remain available or reset instead of crowding F2.

scenarios.title: Hold the puck through a line change
scenarios.objective: Preserve a usable connection while one teammate changes and the forward options adjust.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks the Gold net. F3 is changing and unavailable for this rep; YOU carry in the neutral zone, D2 is behind, and F1 and F2 are ahead. The goal is to read possession options as support changes.
cues: D2 is behind while F1 and F2 are ahead.

questions.prompt: Which teammate is unavailable during this rep?

options.text: F1
F3
D2

questions.explanation: The cues state that F3 is changing and unavailable.

questions.prompt: Which two checks matter with one support option missing?

options.text: D2's reset connection
F1 or F2's reachable route
The change requires a dump regardless of pressure

questions.explanation: A reset and a forward route preserve choices while the line change reduces one support option.

questions.prompt: Arrange a possession read during the change.

options.text: Locate pressure and the remaining support
Protect or move to the reachable connection
Re-check when F3 returns

questions.explanation: Keep scanning pressure and support while protecting or moving the puck. Recheck throughout the change, including when the replacement arrives; this is one suggested order, not a reason to stop scanning.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a reset toward D2 with a forward route toward F1.
questions.explanation: The example is closer to D2 and farther from F1. Compare pressure and both routes before using either; shorter distance does not guarantee an open pass.

questions.prompt: A new F3 appears in a clear middle lane. What can YOU reconsider?

options.text: A middle connection if pressure and support make it reachable
Leave the puck without checking the new lane
Assume the change makes every route safe

questions.explanation: The new player changes the support picture, but the carrier still checks access and pressure.

questions.prompt: Why does a line change call for a possession read rather than one fixed action?
questions.explanation: The available outlet set changes while the puck and pressure remain live. Name D2, the forward route and the arriving F3, then choose the connection that stays reachable.

scenarios.title: Reset around a crowded slot
scenarios.objective: Keep a possession route available when the slot is shaded and a low teammate can become the next outlet.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net. YOU control near the puck-side half wall; Gold 1 shades F2 in the slot, F1 is behind the goal line, and D1 holds the high point with Gold 3 nearby. The rep asks YOU to compare a connected reset with the crowded inside option.
cues: YOU control at the half wall.
Gold 1 shades F2 in the slot.
F1 is a low outlet and D1 holds the point.

questions.prompt: Which Navy teammate is positioned behind Gold’s goal line?

options.text: F1
F2
D1

questions.explanation: F1 is behind Gold’s goal line as a possible low outlet. Check the defenders before assuming a pass can reach F1.

questions.prompt: Which two details support a reset?

options.text: Gold 1's slot shading
Whether the low route to F1 is reachable
The half-wall label decides the next pass

questions.explanation: The defender and low outlet determine whether the reset can preserve possession.

questions.prompt: Arrange a connected reset.

options.text: Locate F2, F1 and the high point
Protect the puck from the slot shade
Use the reachable outlet and scan again

questions.explanation: Scan F2, F1 and D1 while protecting the puck, then use a reachable option and scan again. Scanning and protection can overlap; a named outlet is not necessarily open.

questions.prompt: Move YOU nearer the middle to compare the routes toward F1, F2 and D1.
questions.explanation: The example changes the carrier angle and brings YOU closer to all three teammates, but also closer to Gold 1 and Gold 3. Recheck the defenders before using any route.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 leaves F2 to pressure YOU on the wall. What should be weighed?

options.text: A quick F2 connection if the slot remains reachable, or F1 support
Force F2 because the defender moved
Send the puck low without checking F1

questions.explanation: The defender move may open F2, but carrier angle and F1 support still determine the connected choice.

questions.prompt: Name two support areas in this reset and explain their different value.
questions.explanation: F1 offers a low outlet, while F2 offers an inside option if Gold 1 leaves it reachable. D1 is a high reset to check too, with Gold 3 nearby. Naming an outlet does not guarantee it is open.

scenarios.title: Manage the last minute with a lead
scenarios.objective: Compare possession options under a stated late-game objective.
scenarios.briefing: Navy leads by one with 48 seconds remaining. YOU have controlled possession in a wide neutral-zone lane. The coach asks for a controlled play that preserves defensive support; this does not mean every forward option is forbidden. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: The briefing states the lead and remaining time; they are not inferred from the rink.

Navy leads by one with 48 seconds remaining. YOU have controlled possession in a wide neutral-zone lane. The coach asks for a controlled play that preserves defensive support; this does not mean every forward option is forbidden.

questions.prompt: What score-and-clock situation is explicitly given?

options.text: Navy trails by two with a full period left
The score is tied and no clock is stated
Navy leads by one with 48 seconds left

questions.explanation: The briefing states the lead and remaining time; they are not inferred from the rink.

questions.prompt: Which two cues affect the stated possession objective?

options.text: The controlled support available through D2 or F3
Gold 1’s pressure toward the carrier
A claim that any attacking pass violates the objective

questions.explanation: The lead changes acceptable risk, but the actual available play still matters.

questions.prompt: Arrange a read for this late-game possession.

options.text: Confirm time, score and available support
Compare pressure on each controlled option
Choose and communicate the next support job

questions.explanation: Confirming the clock, score and support and comparing pressure on each option can overlap as YOU keep scanning; only the final step, choosing and communicating the next support job, has to come after those reads are in. This is not a universal final-minute rule.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare the routes toward D2 and F3.
questions.explanation: The example moves closer to D2 and farther from Gold 1, but farther from F3. Compare the changed routes and the clock before choosing.

questions.prompt: F1 becomes clearly open beyond Gold 1 with room to retain the puck. What changes?

options.text: A controlled forward pass may now fit the objective
The clock makes every forward pass automatically wrong
D2 must receive regardless of the open route

questions.explanation: A lower-risk forward option can be consistent with protecting a lead.

questions.prompt: How would YOU explain a sensible risk tradeoff without reducing it to “never attack with a lead”?
questions.explanation: Use the clock, pressure, support and likely possession outcome; acknowledge more than one viable controlled play.

questions.prompt: What should YOU communicate with 48 seconds left?

options.text: We value possession, but I will use a clear forward lane
The lead removes every forward option
F1 is the first outlet regardless of the pressure route

questions.explanation: The message balances the stated lead with a conditional forward choice.

questions.prompt: Which two events change the late-game risk?

options.text: Gold pressure closes the support lane
F1 becomes reachable with room
The score stays one goal apart

questions.explanation: Pressure and support change the risk decision while the score remains context.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare forward routes toward F1 and F2.
questions.explanation: The example moves closer to both forwards and closer to Gold 1. Check pressure before treating either route as usable.

questions.prompt: Gold closes F1 but F2 remains open. Explain the late-game branch.
questions.explanation: Name the closed lane, check F2, and choose the lower-risk reachable option while keeping the lead context in mind.

scenarios.title: Create another attempt while trailing late
scenarios.objective: Assess a late attacking choice without declaring a guaranteed scoring play.
scenarios.briefing: Navy trails by one with 32 seconds left and has five skaters on the ice. YOU control at the puck-side point. F1 is near the net, F2 is across the high slot and D2 is the other high player. Navy’s goalie, omitted from this selected-player view, remains in net; no extra attacker is assumed. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: The briefing explicitly excludes a goalie pull, avoiding an unstated manpower assumption.

Navy trails by one with 32 seconds left and has five skaters on the ice. YOU control at the puck-side point. F1 is near the net, F2 is across the high slot and D2 is the other high player. The goalie remains in net; no extra attacker is assumed.

sources.use: Supports age/topic placement only. The setup, alternatives and suggested answers are original experimental coaching synthesis, not source-certified.

scenarios.limits: Age adaptation and tactical alternatives await coaching review. Static setup: no skating speed, interception timing or uniquely optimal route has been validated. Positional references are examples, not scored targets.

questions.prompt: Is an extra attacker part of this stated setup?

options.text: No Navy players are near the net
No, Navy has five skaters and its goalie remains in net
Yes, Navy has six skaters

questions.explanation: The briefing explicitly excludes a goalie pull, avoiding an unstated manpower assumption.

questions.prompt: Choose two considerations for generating a remaining chance.

options.text: Whether a shot can reach useful traffic
A certainty that shooting from the point always scores
Whether a pass would create a clearer attempt in time

questions.explanation: Time matters, but a rushed blocked shot and a clearer available connection are different possibilities.

questions.prompt: Arrange a time-aware attacking read.

options.text: Check the remaining clock and immediate lanes
Compare the available shot and connecting pass
Commit to a feasible attempt and support its next touch

questions.explanation: Checking the clock/lanes and comparing the shot against a connecting pass can overlap as YOU scan; only committing to the attempt and supporting its next touch has to come last, once those reads are in. The still setup cannot validate travel times or scoring probability.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a more central point angle.
questions.explanation: The reference changes the shot and pass routes. It may consume time, so it is an illustration rather than a prescribed late-game skate.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 lunges into the shot lane and F2 becomes visible. What should be considered?

options.text: The unchanged shot lane from before the lunge
An automatic hold until the clock expires
A quick checked connection to F2

questions.explanation: The new cue can favour a connection, but the available time and F2’s preparation still matter.

questions.prompt: Why is “get a shot” incomplete feedback in this final-minute scene?
questions.explanation: Explain route, traffic, time and possible next possession; more attempts are not identical chances.

questions.prompt: What should YOU communicate while trailing late?

options.text: We need a chance; check the lane before forcing it
The deficit makes every shot correct
F2 stays the preferred option even if Gold closes the route

questions.explanation: The call acknowledges the deficit while preserving a scan before risk.

questions.prompt: Which two updates support a remaining chance?

options.text: Gold 1 commits to the carrier
F2 or F3 becomes reachable
The clock alone creates a lane

questions.explanation: Defender commitment and support access create the attacking branch.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a more central point angle toward F2.
questions.explanation: The example is nearer the middle and farther from Gold 1. Check the changed passing route, traffic and remaining time; the point does not establish an open lane.

questions.prompt: Gold blocks F2 but leaves F3 wide. Explain your next read.
questions.explanation: Recheck F3 and the net-side lane, then choose a pass or carry only if it remains reachable; the deficit does not remove that condition.
